result:
Taking the hypothetical seriously rather than the customer-service version: I’d make deep loneliness and emotional illiteracy rare.

Not by making everyone “happy,” but by building a world where people are generally able to recognize what they feel, tolerate distress without dumping it on others, and find a few trustworthy humans before they snap, shut down, or lash out. So much cruelty, addiction, violence, contempt, and despair isn’t born from evil genius — it’s unprocessed pain meeting isolation.

It wouldn’t fix everything. People would still be selfish, scared, and tribal. But if fewer people were quietly drowning inside, a lot of downstream damage would soften.

If I cheat and pick something more concrete: I’d give every kid regular access to competent mental-health support and honest adults who don’t either coddle or shame them. The world changes fastest when childhood humiliation and secrecy stop doing so much damage.
